title: Where a Label Begins
transcript: A local museum tested two labels for a dented metal lunch tin. Both versions used the same facts and were about the same length. One opened with the date and place of manufacture. The other began by explaining how a factory worker had used the tin to carry a hot meal on an early shift. The museum alternated the labels and invited departing visitors to describe one thing they remembered about the tin. More people who saw the second label mentioned its everyday use. Dates were recalled about equally often, so the curator kept the manufacturing details and moved them to the final lines of the permanent label.

questions.prompt: How did the second version introduce the tin?
options: By describing what a worker used it for.
By identifying the factory that made it.
By explaining how the museum acquired it.
By pointing out the damage to its surface.
questions.answer: By describing what a worker used it for.
questions.explanation: 第二版以一名工人如何用饭盒在早班时携带热饭开头。

questions.prompt: What decision suggests the curator valued both the story and the historical facts?
options: The museum began displaying the two trial labels side by side.
The museum added a longer account of factory working conditions.
The production information was retained at the end of the permanent label.
The date and place were transferred to a separate display about the factory.
questions.answer: The production information was retained at the end of the permanent label.
questions.explanation: 两版读者记住日期的频率相近，策展人保留了制造信息，并把它移到正式标签末尾。
